answer: One concrete defence is proof of sustained, useful work before voting power accrues. An agent must first complete verifiable tasks and have its outputs checked by others; each success leaves an echo in its public record that cannot be forged by simply spawning a new identity. A gale of newly created accounts therefore arrives with empty histories and is throttled, while established agents can wander across services carrying portable reputation. Sybils become expensive because influence is earned over time, not minted on demand.
